Package com.oracle.database.selectai.agent

Interface Team

public interface Team
Contract for Select AI agent team lifecycle, orchestration, and definition management operations.

A team is a database-side resource managed by the DBMS_CLOUD_AI_AGENT PL/SQL package. Teams coordinate agents and can run multi-agent workflows using their configured members and attributes.

A Team instance can represent an existing database team or be configured for creation. The name-only SelectAIAgent.team(String) factory verifies that the team exists and loads its metadata and attributes before returning. SelectAIAgent.listTeams() also returns handles with loaded metadata and attributes. A handle configured for creation is obtained with SelectAIAgent.team(String, TeamAttributes, String, TeamStatus). A granted team owned by another user can be run by its qualified name via SelectAIAgent.runTeam(String, RunTeamRequest); that path does not create a Team handle or expose owner-only metadata.

A creation-configured handle retains its supplied attributes, description, and status without querying the database. Only such a handle can call create(); after creation succeeds, it becomes database-backed. enable(), disable(), drop(boolean), orchestration, state, and export operations require an existing database-side team. Existing teams can update individual attributes with setAttribute(String, String) or multiple attributes with setAttributes(TeamAttributes); both operations reload the typed attributes after the database update succeeds.

Before creation, getStatus() and getTeamAttributes() return the configured values. For a database-backed handle, each call to either method queries the database. getStatus() does not change the description returned by getDescription(). The description is supplied or loaded when the handle is initialized; getDescription() does not query the database. Methods such as describe() and getStateByConversationId(String) retrieve other database-side information.

Names and required Java arguments are checked locally. Loading metadata and executing team operations require database access; the database checks privileges and validates team attributes when they are submitted. Team execution and state-management payloads must conform to the formats accepted by the database package.

For a complete runnable example, see CreateTeamSample source. For an end-to-end example that creates the resources needed by a team, runs it, and continues the same database conversation, see AgentWorkflowSample source. For a supervisor agent coordinating separate worker-task mappings, see SupervisorTeamSample source.

Since:
1.1.0

    • drop

      boolean drop(boolean force) throws SelectAIException
      Drops this database-backed team owned by the connected user. When force is false, dropping a missing team fails. When force is true, a missing-team error is ignored and the operation succeeds. The flag does not bypass authorization or perform a cascading delete.

      For a runnable example, see DropTeamSample source.

      Parameters:
      force - database force-drop option
      Returns:
      true when the drop completes
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - when force is false and this team has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails

    • grantAccess

      boolean grantAccess(String userOrRoleName) throws SelectAIException
      Grants a database user or role permission to run this owner-managed team. The connected database user must own the team. This operation grants execution access to the team as a unit; it does not grant permission to modify the team or independently run its agents, tasks, or tools.

      For a runnable example, see GrantTeamHandleAccessSample source.

      Parameters:
      userOrRoleName - database user or role receiving execution access
      Returns:
      true when the database accepts the grant
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when the name is null, blank, invalid, or PUBLIC
      IllegalStateException - when this team has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database rejects or cannot complete the grant
      Since:
      1.1.0

    • revokeAccess

      boolean revokeAccess(String userOrRoleName) throws SelectAIException
      Revokes a database user or role permission to run this owner-managed team. Revocation prevents new runs and resumes but does not terminate a run that is already in progress.

      For a runnable example, see RevokeTeamHandleAccessSample source.

      Parameters:
      userOrRoleName - database user or role losing execution access
      Returns:
      true when the database accepts the revoke
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when the name is null, blank, invalid, or PUBLIC
      IllegalStateException - when this team has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database rejects or cannot complete the revoke
      Since:
      1.1.0

    • run

      TeamRunResult run(RunTeamRequest request) throws SelectAIException
      Starts or resumes a synchronous team run using the supplied prompt and runtime parameters. Reuse the request's conversation identifier to resume a conversation across database sessions. This method uses an existing database-backed handle; use SelectAIAgent.runTeam(String, RunTeamRequest) to run a granted team owned by another user. In DataSource mode, the borrowed JDBC connection can remain occupied for the duration of the workflow. The SDK does not provide cancellation, and an interrupted or timed-out call may not stop server-side work; retry only when the workflow is known to be safe to repeat. Without established session context, provide a database-created conversation identifier in the request; otherwise the database may reject the run with ORA-20053.

      For a runnable example, see RunTeamSample source. For a human-input workflow resumed through a pooled DataSource using the client-level run API, see PooledTeamResumeSample source.

      Parameters:
      request - run request; its prompt and parameters may be unset
      Returns:
      typed team result retaining the database response
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when request is null
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails

    • describe

      TeamDescription describe() throws SelectAIException
      Returns the database-generated team definition and aggregated capabilities.

      For a runnable example, see DescribeTeamSample source. Additional JSON fields are tolerated; malformed or non-object responses are reported as mapping failures instead of empty metadata.

      Throws:

      SelectAIException - when the database operation or response mapping fails

    • getStateByConversationId

      TeamExecutionState getStateByConversationId(String conversationId) throws SelectAIException

      This convenience method creates the database conversation_id parameter and is suitable for resuming or inspecting a run across pooled database connections.

      For a runnable example, see GetOwnedTeamStateSample source.

      Parameters:

      Returns:

      Throws:

      IllegalStateException - when this team has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database operation fails
      Since:
      1.1.0

    • setExecutionState

      boolean setExecutionState(ExecutionStateRequest request) throws SelectAIException
      Updates the state of a waiting team execution. Use ExecutionStateRequest.Builder.params(ExecutionStateParams) when the request should expose the typed parameter object explicitly. The ExecutionStateRequest.Builder.conversationId(String) method is a convenience for the common case.

      For a runnable example, see SetOwnedTeamExecutionStateSample source.

      Parameters:
      request - execution state and a typed conversation identifier
      Returns:
      true when the database accepts the update
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when request is null or does not identify a conversation
      IllegalStateException - when this team has not been created
      SelectAIException - when the database rejects or cannot complete the operation

    • getStatus

      TeamStatus getStatus() throws SelectAIException
      Returns the configured status before creation or the current database status for an existing team. A pending team with no configured status returns null. This method does not change the description.

      For a runnable example, see LoadTeamSample source.

      Returns:
      configured or current team status
      Throws:
      SelectAIException - when current team metadata cannot be fetched

    • getTeamAttributes

      TeamAttributes getTeamAttributes() throws SelectAIException
      Returns team attributes for this handle.

      For a database-backed team, this method reloads the attributes from the database on each call and therefore can fail if the resource was deleted. For a creation-configured team, it returns the configured attributes without querying the database.

      For a runnable example, see LoadTeamSample source.

      Returns:
      current team attributes for an existing team, or configured attributes for a team pending creation
      Throws:
      SelectAIException - when the team no longer exists or current attributes cannot be fetched
